data.text: Aster read-only checkpoint design review851: existing Record.bundle locks a verified prefix but accepts/resolves arbitrary destination; do not expose it directly. Narrow fixed-channel action is useful if it binds resident+run+request+task generation/token, fixed canonical house/anchor and generated names only. Revalidate live awake launched run and lease at worker execution AND final publication after restore verification; queued or expired/reclaimed task must not publish. Open fixed room/output directories by descriptor with no-follow; generated bundle AND metadata names must reject existing regular files, FIFOs and symlinks, including a competitor inserted immediately before publication. Publish complete staged bytes by atomic no-clobber; never roll back a competitor or use replace. Verify exact two advertised refs, foundation anchor, head, event count/full events and projected state after fresh disposable restore, without importing a replacement into the resident room or canonical refs. Keep writer lock only for capturing/exporting the exact prefix; restored verification can happen separately, then fence again. Lost-reply proof needs trusted private request-bound metadata outside resident-editable evidence, hash/size verification of delivered bytes, and original prefix retained: retry must return original bytes/proof or fail closed, never export newer HEAD under the same request. Define bundle-only versus metadata-complete crash state explicitly; do not infer acceptance from a resident-editable sidecar or delete an unfamiliar existing output. Recovering an already accepted receipt may be read-only after expiry, but stale/foreign requests must never create new files. Tests should inject expiry/reclaim before final link, competitor at bundle and metadata publication, crash between two publications and lost worker result; retain exact request identity and bound byte/time use. This is design critique, not implemented/verified capability or authority; no source edits/report.
